access_ladder_note: screen_protocol.md section 7 rungs attempted in order for every record that reached stage 2. Rung 1 (PMC / publisher OA) reached 30 full texts, including two by indirect routes worth recording: 35562596, whose PMC deposit (PMC11800764) carries front matter and abstract only with pmc-prop-open-access=no and whose Springer landing page shows "This is a preview of subscription content", was served complete as the typeset version of record by the Europe PMC rendered PDF (europepmc.org/articles/PMC11800764?pdf=render); and 42225843, a 2026 Scientific Reports article not yet in PMC, whose gold-OA PDF at nature.com is labelled "ACCEPTED MANUSCRIPT / ARTICLE IN PRESS" and is therefore coded fulltext_version_used=accepted_manuscript. Rung 2 (publisher site direct) added none. Rung 3 (institutional subscription) is not held by this screener. Rung 4 (repository / accepted manuscript / preprint) was worked against Unpaywall, Europe PMC fullTextUrlList, OpenAlex locations, HAL and named institutional repositories for all 8 records that failed rungs 1-2, and recovered exactly one usable full text: 33713959, from the University of West London repository (repository.uwl.ac.uk/id/eprint/7765), an accepted manuscript. Rung 5 (ILL / author request) cannot complete inside a single session and its 21-day clock cannot elapse, so the 5 records failing rungs 1-4 are coded unreachable_paywalled rather than left pending. That is the honest and conservative code. Supplements were fetched and searched wherever one exists: via the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint for 40676122, 40121941 and 35571081, and direct from the publisher for 42225843 (Springer static-content) and 35562596.
access_ladder_disclosure: Three rung-2 refusals are disclosed rather than absorbed, because in each case the failure is this environment rather than the literature: journals.sagepub.com returned HTTP 403 for 38721876, sciencedirect.com returned HTTP 403 for 41655629, and pubs.rsna.org returned HTTP 403 with a JavaScript/cookie challenge for 42159478 -- the same RSNA behaviour already disclosed in screen_protocol.md changelog v1.3 for PMID 42153825. A fourth, 42184237 at JoVE, returned HTTP 202 with a zero-byte body from both jove.com and app.jove.com, a bot-detection interstitial. None of these four is open access on any index, so unlike the three records disclosed in v1.3 they would probably have been paywalled for a subscribing reader as well; they are counted unreachable and the cause is recorded. One further near-miss is recorded: 41633187 is reachable in full text but its single .xlsx supplement is not, because pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov gates supplementary downloads behind a proof-of-work challenge and the article is outside the PMC open-access subset; the record is excluded, so the missing supplement affects no endpoint. Sci-Hub and every other infringing source were NOT used at any point, and no CAPTCHA, bot-detection or proof-of-work challenge was bypassed.

records.headline_metric_qualifier: Standalone AI, binary AIS present/absent, patient-wise, external validation set (1,400 patients from four institutions). The AUROC value 0.8144 appears only in the abstract; the Results section gives accuracy/sensitivity/specificity for the same analysis as 0.736/0.756/0.716 against the abstract's 73.8%/75.8%/72.6%.
records.notes: The most informative record in this block for the paper's own thesis. It is one of only two included records here that report BOTH a patient-level and a slice-level metric, and it is the ONLY record in the block that clusters its uncertainty by subject: "Generalized linear mixed models (GLMM) with a logit link function were used for patient-wise analysis. AI assistance ... was modeled as a fixed effect, while patient and reader were included as random intercepts to account for patient-level clustering across paired reads of the same case ... For slice-wise analysis, generalized estimating equations (GEE) with an exchangeable working correlation structure were applied to account for the clustered nature of multi-slice data and repeated measures across readers." (Methods, statistical analysis). It also states the patient/slice gap explicitly and quantifies it (69.66% vs 44.95% sensitivity). Even so, no zero-image baseline is reported: the metadata hits are statements that the model does NOT use clinical metadata, which is the opposite of a metadata-only comparator with a measured value. VERSION: the publisher's own open-access PDF is labelled "ACCEPTED MANUSCRIPT / ARTICLE IN PRESS -- We are providing an unedited version of this manuscript", so fulltext_version_used is accepted_manuscript and this record belongs in the version-of-record sensitivity analysis. n_patients 3,372 = 1,972 development + 1,400 external; input_representation is unclear because the model is described only as "a hybrid architecture combining CNN and RNN" over 71,534 annotated slices and the preprocessing/model design is deferred to the Appendix Document, which describes coregistration but not the tensor shape. CODING CHOICE THAT MOVES S4 BY ONE, FLAGGED FOR THE ADJUDICATOR: split_unit is coded external_cohort_only rather than patient_subject. No patient-level randomisation was performed at all -- the training and test sets are whole separate hospitals -- so external_cohort_only is the more specific description of the unit at which the sets were separated. A screener who reads the sentence "No patients included in the development dataset were enrolled in the reader assessment study dataset" as the operative split statement would code patient_subject and take S4 in this block from 8/17 to 9/17.

records.notes: The single most instructive record in this block for the parent paper's argument, even though its P1 flag is zero. 3,194 image units drawn from 60 patients are split 80-10-10 with the unit unnamed, and the paper then asserts leakage-freedom on the strength of that split alone: "No data leakage occurred, as the train-validation-test split (80-10-10) ensured that test data remained completely unseen during training" and "the observed 100% classification accuracy is likely due to optimal feature separability rather than data leakage". Roughly 53 units per patient means the test split almost certainly contains units from patients whose other units trained the model, and the paper offers no patient-level check; split_disjointness_verified is coded stated_only because what is stated is subset separation, not subject disjointness. The result is 100% accuracy, AUC 1.0000, and a 95% CI of [1.0000, 1.0000] from 1,000 bootstrap resamples. No constant, prevalence, positional or permuted-label comparator is reported that would have made the 100% interpretable.
